dedupe_keys.name: iceye open sar data open synthetic aperture radar imagery

description: ICEYE, which operates a large constellation of synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellites, publishes a curated selection of its SAR imagery as open data for research, innovation and education. Radar imaging works regardless of time of day or weather, which suits monitoring of floods, disasters and infrastructure. The data can be reached in three ways without registration or payment: an Open SAR Data map browser to filter by location, imaging mode and acquisition date; a STAC browser to query metadata, preview acquisitions and download assets in standard formats including SLC, GRD and COG; and the AWS Registry of Open Data, where the archive sits in an S3 bucket that can be read with standard tools and no authentication. The AWS registry states that the data is released under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence, that new data is added frequently, and gives a citation form and product documentation. Caveats: the open set is a selection of acquisitions chosen by ICEYE, not systematic coverage, and SAR products need specialist processing. Coverage is worldwide, at the sites chosen. It supports hazard exposure analysis such as flood extent and damage mapping around infrastructure; related records are DLR EOC Geoservice, CNES GEODES and JAXA G-Portal.
